A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GUI-CURSOR research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and expanded evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GUI-CURSOR results on ScreenSpot-v2 and ScreenSpot-Pro, alongside ablations, training analyses and the cursor-in-box experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds grounding benchmarks, online agent evaluation, spatial-reasoning tests, additional backbones, efficiency measurements and crop-failure analysis.

M1.justification: The cursor-control procedure, history conditioning, GRPO objective, four trajectory penalties and cursor-centric focusing remain unchanged. Additional backbones use the retained procedure. Appendix L discusses dragging as a future extension rather than an implemented modification.

E1.justification: v2 adds OSWorld-G and UI-Vision grounding, online OSWorld interaction, SpatialMQA and SPHERE spatial reasoning, and cropped-image target-presence classification. This substantially expands task and domain coverage beyond the retained ScreenSpot benchmarks and cursor-in-box test. Training sources remain Aria-UI and OS-Atlas.

E2.justification: The original ScreenSpot comparator sets are retained. v2 adds reported comparisons with GUI-Spotlight in Tables 2 and 7, RegionFocus in Table 10, Qwen3-VL models in Table 11, and o3 and GTA1-32B in the OSWorld comparison, substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds UI-TARS-1.5-7B and Qwen3-VL-2B-Thinking training configurations, o3-based online evaluation with explicit action budgets, timed inference comparisons and binary target-presence testing. The original training hyperparameters remain unchanged. OSWorld results use different action budgets across methods, so they are not equal-budget comparisons.

E4.justification: The original reward, thinking, focusing and training-dynamics analyses are retained. New analyses investigate spatial transfer beyond GUI images, training and inference efficiency, test-time compute trade-offs, applicability to Qwen3 backbones and detection of targets excluded by cropping. The original case studies are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The added results continue point-estimate reporting. GRPO trajectory sampling and reward normalization do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original Qwen-based ScreenSpot results remain 93.9% and 56.5%. New results include 58.1% ScreenSpot-Pro accuracy with UI-TARS initialization, 57.1% OSWorld accuracy with o3 at 50 steps, 43.4% on SpatialMQA, and 55.0% ScreenSpot-Pro accuracy for GUI-CURSOR-2B. v2 also adds timing and crop-detection outcomes and replaces ScreenSpot-v2 text/icon breakdowns with platform averages.

T1.justification: The bounding-box formulation, distance reward, penalty definitions and GRPO mathematics are retained, with equation renumbering and formatting changes. No substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes state-of-the-art results on two grounding benchmarks and adaptive cursor movement. v2 broadens the headline contributions to agentic performance, superior performance with matched backbones and less training data, and spatial-reasoning generalization beyond GUI images. The interactive-grounding contribution remains central.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning spatial transfer, latency–accuracy trade-offs, historical visual context mitigating cursor occlusion, and limitations to click-style grounding. Appendix J extends the existing crop limitation with the implications of 31% missing-target detection and 20% false positives, explaining why reliable recovery would require further training.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands resource and evaluation documentation: 8K training samples, per-update and rollout timings, throughput, latency accounting for rendering and history encoding, same-hardware RegionFocus evaluation, and the exact target-presence prompt. The original optimizer settings, GPU configuration, rollout details and system prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices G–H substantially expand positioning against iterative cropping and test-time scaling, discussing GUI-Spotlight, GUI-ARP, GUI-RC/RCPO and RegionFocus. Appendix L adds GUI-Drag. These comparisons clarify the distinction between learning cursor-based spatial alignment and narrowing image regions.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary and conclusion are selectively rewritten. Spatial discussion moves from Section 4 to Section 3.3, and implementation appendices are reorganized. The LLM-use disclosure is removed, while impact and acknowledgement sections are added. Most retained technical prose remains closely preserved.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper. Existing figure panels are split or relocated, ScreenSpot-v2 table columns are consolidated, and new tables present agentic, spatial, efficiency and backbone comparisons. Original workflow graphics, plots and case-study images are retained within the redesigned layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow evidence for practical utility and generality through online OSWorld evaluation, non-GUI spatial benchmarks and additional backbones. Appendices F and J quantify runtime trade-offs and crop-recovery limitations, making the method more assessable. These gains outweigh reduced ScreenSpot-v2 subgroup detail and a localized reporting inconsistency: Table 11 attributes 58.1%/65.6% to a Qwen-based model, whereas Tables 1–2 associate those results with UI-TARS initialization.
